title: Taiwan's Inflation Stays Above 2% for a Sixth Month
summaryZh: 台灣10月CPI漲2.33%，連續第六個月高於2%
summaryHi: ताइवान में अक्टूबर की महँगाई 2.33% रही, लगातार छठे महीने 2% से ऊपर
summaryEs: La inflación de Taiwán fue del 2,33 % en octubre, sexto mes seguido por encima del 2 %
summaryJa: 台湾の10月CPIは2.33％上昇、6カ月連続で2％超え
summaryEn: Taiwan's consumer prices rose 2.33% in October, easing from September but above 2% for a sixth month.
paragraphs: Inflation in Taiwan eased slightly in October but remained above the central bank's 2% target for a sixth consecutive month, according to figures released on Thursday by the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS).
The consumer price index rose 2.33% year on year, down from 2.74% in September, which had been a 31-month high. Core inflation, which leaves out fresh fruit, vegetables and energy, stood at 2.23%.

Transport and communication costs climbed 4.36%, driven mainly by a 15.17% rise in fuel prices and a 12.53% increase in airfares. Egg prices surged 11.45%, while the cost of eating out rose 3.01%, the fifth straight month at or above 3%.
Several factors held the overall figure down. Vegetable prices began to fall, and the year-on-year increase in electricity rates was smaller than in previous months.

However, DGBAS official Tsai Hsiu-hui warned that the relief may be short-lived. She said November's inflation rate was likely to stay above 2% and could be slightly higher than October's, although she stressed that prices were rising only moderately.
Prices in Taiwan are still going up. In October, prices were 2.33% higher than one year before.
This number is lower than in September. Then it was 2.74%. But it is still over 2%. The central bank wants prices to grow by less than 2% a year. Prices have been over this line for six months now.
Some things cost a lot more. Petrol cost 15% more, and plane tickets cost 12.5% more. Eggs cost over 11% more. Eating at restaurants also cost more.
Vegetables got cheaper in October. Electricity prices also went up more slowly.
A government statistics office shares these numbers every month. An official there said prices may stay over 2% in November too.

paragraphs: Prices in Taiwan kept rising in October, but a little more slowly than before. The consumer price index (CPI), which measures the cost of everyday goods and services, was 2.33% higher than a year earlier.

In September, the figure was 2.74%, the highest in more than two and a half years. Even so, October was the sixth month in a row above 2%. This is the level that Taiwan's central bank sees as a warning line.
Transport was one of the biggest reasons. Fuel cost 15.17% more than a year ago, and air tickets were 12.53% more expensive. Egg prices jumped 11.45%, and eating out cost 3.01% more.
Some prices helped to slow inflation. Vegetables became cheaper, and electricity bills did not rise as fast as before.
Tsai Hsiu-hui, an official at the statistics agency, said prices in November would probably stay above 2%. She added that they might even rise a little faster than in October.

The consumer price index rose 2.33% year on year, down from 2.74% in September, which had been a 31-month high. Core inflation, which leaves out fresh fruit, vegetables and energy, stood at 2.23%.

paragraphs: Taiwan's inflation cooled marginally in October, yet it stayed above the central bank's 2% threshold for the sixth month running, official data published on Thursday showed.

According to the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS), the consumer price index climbed 2.33% from a year earlier, retreating from September's 2.74%, the steepest rate in 31 months. Core inflation, which strips out volatile items such as fresh produce and energy, came in at 2.23%.

Transport remained the chief source of pressure. Fuel costs jumped 15.17% and airfares 12.53%, lifting the transport and communication category by 4.36%. Households also faced pricier eggs, up 11.45%, and dining-out costs that have now risen by at least 3% for five consecutive months.

The slowdown owed much to cheaper vegetables and a narrower annual increase in electricity tariffs. Producer prices, by contrast, soared almost 20% year on year, a sign that cost pressures further up the supply chain have yet to fade.

DGBAS official Tsai Hsiu-hui cautioned that November's figure would probably remain above 2% and might edge higher. Nevertheless, she described the overall rise in prices as moderate and said Taiwan was not facing a problem of imported inflation.
sentZh: 週四公布的官方數據顯示，台灣十月通膨略為降溫，但仍連續第六個月高於央行2%的門檻。
根據行政院主計總處，消費者物價指數較一年前上升2.33%，低於九月的2.74%，即31個月來最大的漲幅。
剔除新鮮農產品與能源等波動大項目的核心通膨為2.23%。
交通仍是壓力的主要來源。
燃料成本跳升15.17%，機票上漲12.53%，使交通及通訊類別上漲4.36%。
家庭也面臨更貴的雞蛋，漲了11.45%，而外食費用已連續五個月上漲至少3%。
漲勢放緩主要歸功於蔬菜變便宜，以及電價年增幅縮小。
相較之下，生產者物價年增近20%，顯示供應鏈上游的成本壓力尚未消退。
主計總處官員蔡秀慧提醒，十一月的數字可能仍高於2%，且可能小幅走高。
儘管如此，她形容整體物價漲幅溫和，並表示台灣並未面臨輸入性通膨問題。

paragraphs: Consumer price inflation in Taiwan moderated slightly in October, but it nonetheless exceeded the central bank's 2% benchmark for a sixth successive month, according to statistics released on Thursday.

The Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics (DGBAS) reported that the consumer price index rose 2.33% year on year, a noticeable decline from September's 2.74%, which had represented a 31-month peak. Core inflation, a measure that excludes fresh fruit, vegetables and energy, was recorded at 2.23%.

The most substantial upward pressure came from transport. Fuel prices escalated by 15.17% and airfares by 12.53%, pushing the transport and communication category up 4.36%. Meanwhile, eggs became 11.45% more expensive, and the cost of dining out increased by 3.01%, marking the fifth consecutive month at or above 3%.

This modest easing was largely attributable to declining vegetable prices and a less pronounced annual rise in electricity tariffs. Wholesale indicators, however, painted a more concerning picture: producer prices surged by almost a fifth compared with a year earlier.

Looking ahead, DGBAS official Tsai Hsiu-hui anticipated that inflation would remain above 2% in November and could be marginally higher than in October. Even so, she maintained that the increase in prices was moderate and that Taiwan was not experiencing imported inflation.
sentZh: 根據週四公布的統計，台灣消費者物價通膨十月略為放緩，但仍連續第六個月超過央行2%的基準。
行政院主計總處公布，消費者物價指數年增2.33%，較九月的2.74%明顯下降，而九月的數字是31個月來的高峰。
排除新鮮蔬果與能源的核心通膨為2.23%。
最大的上漲壓力來自交通。
燃料價格上升15.17%，機票上升12.53%，推動交通及通訊類別上漲4.36%。
同時，雞蛋貴了11.45%，外食費用上漲3.01%，已連續第五個月漲幅達3%以上。
這次小幅緩和主要可歸因於蔬菜價格下跌，以及電價年增幅較不明顯。
然而，批發面的指標呈現出更令人擔憂的景象：生產者物價較一年前大漲近五分之一。
展望未來，主計總處官員蔡秀慧預期十一月通膨仍將高於2%，且可能略高於十月。
即便如此，她仍堅稱物價漲幅溫和，台灣並未出現輸入性通膨。

recorded.ex: The hottest day was recorded in July.

relief.ex: The rain brought relief from the heat.

remain.ex: The roads remain closed after the flood.

remained.ex: The shop remained open all night.

reported.ex: The company reported higher sales this year.

represented.ex: The figure represented a big rise.

restaurants.en: places where you buy and eat meals
restaurants.ex: The new restaurants in town are very busy.

retreating.en: moving back to a lower level
retreating.ex: Oil prices are retreating from last month's high.

rise.ex: There was a rise in prices.

row.en: in a row: one after another
row.ex: They won five games in a row.

running.en: one after another; continuing to work
running.ex: It was the third day running of heavy rain.

said.ex: She said the shop was closed.

sees.ex: She sees the plan as a good idea.

services.ex: The bus service runs every hour.

shares.ex: The office shares new data each week.

showed.ex: She showed her plan to the team.

sign.en: something that shows; sign up = register
sign.ex: Rising rents are a sign of a busy city.

slow.ex: The bank was slow to answer my email.

slowly.ex: The car moved slowly in the snow.

so.en: used in 'even so' meaning despite that

soared.en: rose very quickly to a high level

source.ex: Tourism is a big source of jobs.

statistics.en: numbers that give facts about something
statistics.ex: Statistics show more people cycle to work.

stay.ex: Most tourists stay in the centre.

stayed.en: continued to be in a state

steepest.en: the biggest and fastest (of a rise or fall)
steepest.ex: It was the steepest rise in house prices this year.

still.ex: She is still waiting for the bus.

stood.ex: Unemployment stood at five per cent.

straight.en: one after another without a break
straight.ex: It rained for five straight days.

stressed.en: said strongly that it is important
stressed.ex: She stressed the need for care.

strips.ex: The measure strips out seasonal changes.

substantial.ex: The new road needs a substantial amount of money.

example.en: There has been a substantial rise in rents.

noteEn.meaning: large in size, value or importance.

noteJa.exampleTr: 家賃が大幅に上昇した。

successive.ex: Prices rose for four successive years.

example.en: Sales rose for the third successive year.
example.zh: 銷售額連續第三年上升。

note.usage: 常見 for the + 序數 + successive + 時間；successive governments。

noteEn.meaning: following one after another without a break.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'for the third successive month', 'successive governments'.

noteHi.usage: for the third successive year आम प्रयोग है।

noteEs.exampleTr: Las ventas subieron por tercer año sucesivo.
noteEs.usage: Se usa for the third successive year.

noteJa.exampleTr: 売上は3年連続で増加した。
noteJa.usage: for the third successive year の形が多い。

noteKo.usage: for the third successive year 형태가 흔하다.

supply.ex: The supply of fresh water is limited.

taiwan.en: an island country in East Asia

target.en: a result you plan to achieve
target.ex: The shop met its sales target.

tariffs.en: official prices or charges for a service
tariffs.ex: Electricity tariffs will rise in April.

there.ex: We went to the park and played there.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

things.ex: Put your things in the bag.

threshold.ex: Income above the threshold is taxed.

thursday.ex: The meeting is on Thursday afternoon.

tickets.en: papers or passes to enter a show
tickets.ex: We bought tickets for the show.

transport.en: systems for moving people or goods
transport.ex: Public transport here is cheap and fast.

up.ex: Rents went up again this year.

upward.ex: There is upward pressure on rents.

vegetable.ex: Eat five portions of vegetables a day.

vegetables.ex: Eat five portions of vegetables a day.

wants.ex: She wants a quiet place to study.

warned.ex: Experts warned of a hot summer.

warning.en: a notice that danger may come
warning.ex: The coastguard issued a gale warning.

went.ex: The bill went to parliament last week.

were.ex: The shops were closed on Sunday.

wholesale.en: about selling goods in large amounts to shops
wholesale.ex: Wholesale vegetable prices fell this week.

example.en: Wholesale prices often rise before shop prices.
example.zh: 批發價格往往比零售價格先上漲。

note.usage: 常見 wholesale prices/market；與 retail（零售）相對。

noteEn.meaning: about buying and selling goods in large amounts.

noteHi.exampleTr: थोक कीमतें अक्सर दुकानों की कीमतों से पहले बढ़ती हैं।
noteHi.meaning: बड़ी मात्रा में खरीद-बिक्री से जुड़ा।
noteHi.usage: wholesale prices आम है; उल्टा retail।

noteEs.exampleTr: Los precios mayoristas suelen subir antes que los minoristas.
noteEs.usage: Se usa wholesale prices; lo contrario de retail.

noteJa.exampleTr: 卸売価格は小売価格より先に上がることが多い。
noteJa.usage: wholesale prices の形が多い；反対は retail。

noteKo.usage: wholesale prices 형태가 흔하다; 반대는 retail.

would.ex: A new park would help the town.

year-on-year.en: compared with the same time last year
year-on-year.ex: Sales showed a year-on-year rise of 5 per cent.

yet.ex: They have not yet set a date.
